title: Make Your Functions Return Useful Values
description: Master the fundamental boundary between side-effect logging and explicit function return values in JavaScript. Learn how return statements hand data back to callers, evaluate call expressions, and avoid common undefined bugs.

objectives.statement: Distinguish between returning a value from a function and logging a value to the console.
Predict the value of call expressions when functions explicitly return vs implicitly return undefined.
Refactor JavaScript functions to explicitly return computed values for downstream call expression substitution.

content.title: Make Your Functions Return Useful Values
content.hook: Why does console.log feel like it works, right up until your app breaks?
content.context: In JavaScript, printing text to the screen is a side effect for developers. To pass data to other parts of your code, a function must explicitly return a value.
goals: Distinguish between printing data with console.log() and handing data back with return.
Understand how function calls evaluate to returned values.
Refactor buggy functions that log instead of returning.

content.title: console.log() vs return: What Actually Happens
content.text:
When you call a function, JavaScript creates a local execution frame. The return keyword hands a computed value back to the caller and immediately exits the function frame.

console.log(), by contrast, only writes output to the developer console for debugging and always evaluates to undefined.

If a function finishes executing without an explicit return statement, JavaScript automatically returns undefined.

callout.title: Common Misconception
callout.text: Thinking console.log(x) sends x back to the caller. Assigning const result = logSomething() results in result being undefined!

content.keyTakeaway: Use return to pass data to variables and other functions; use console.log() only for temporary debugging.

content.prompt: What value is stored in receipt after running this code?
content.explanation: calculateTotal uses console.log() to print the total, but lacks a return statement. Functions without a return statement implicitly return undefined. Therefore, receipt receives undefined.

hints.content: Inspect calculateTotal. Does it contain a return statement?
console.log() prints output to the console, but what does it return to receipt?
When a JavaScript function finishes without an explicit return, it evaluates to undefined.

feedback.correct: Spot on! Because calculateTotal lacks a return statement, it implicitly returns undefined, so receipt holds undefined.
feedback.incorrect: Look closely at calculateTotal. Does it have a return statement? If a function finishes without return, what value does it return?

content.title: Refactor utils.js to Return Values
content.prompt: Refactor the helper functions in utils.js so they return computed values instead of logging them.
content.instructions: The utility functions in utils.js currently use console.log() instead of return. Replace console.log() with return in calculateDiscount, formatFullName, and isAdult so they return their computed results to callers.

hints.content: In calculateDiscount, replace console.log(price - discountAmount) with return price - discountAmount.
In formatFullName, return the template string: return `${firstName} ${lastName}`;
In isAdult, return the comparison result: return age >= 18;

feedback.correct: Great job! All functions now return useful values to their callers.
feedback.incorrect: Check your functions. Make sure calculateDiscount, formatFullName, and isAdult use return statements instead of console.log().

content.title: Reflection: return vs console.log()
content.prompt: In your own words, explain the fundamental difference between console.log() and return in JavaScript. Why is relying on console.log() a problem when building real web applications?

feedback.correct: Thank you for sharing your reflection! Understanding the distinction between developer logging and program data flow is critical.
feedback.incorrect: Please write at least 50 characters explaining the difference between return and console.log().

content.title: Function Return Value Mastery
content.summary: You have mastered the mechanics of JavaScript function return values and caller expression substitution.
takeaways: return hands computed values back to the caller and terminates function execution immediately.
console.log() is an I/O side effect for developer inspection, not a data delivery channel.
Functions without explicit return statements implicitly return undefined when called.
Call expressions evaluate directly to their returned values in variable assignments and arithmetic expressions.
